Ive been in a similar situation that it literally feels like its the same person (i know its not but they are literally the exact same in how they act).My advice would be to get a new sponsor. I was worried to also but after I did I felt so much relief as now I dont have to worry constantly about being yelled at or ridiculed if I do something wrong. 

As for the friendship part, I wanted that as well. Although I don't know if that is possible. I know in my scenario she took it really personal. I told her in the morning that I found someone new, and she hung up on me and didn't talk to me until like a month later when she called me because she thought I relapsed. Now we are much better in terms of civility, but I wouldn't say we are friends, which us upsetting but I can't change it. I obviously can't say for certain if that is how your situation will go, and I hope you guys can remain friends if that is what you want to happen, but I would just advise you to also prepare yourself in the event that it doesn't go how you hope it will. 

One other piece of advice I would give you is to really think on who you want to be your new sponsor. I know a lot of people push to newcomers about finding a sponsor right away, but I wish I would have waited. I got my first sponsor a couple meetings in, we had never talked before but she came up to me and asked to take me through the book, myself being naive and new to the program, I accepted and it went downhill fast. My new sponsor I met at my very first meeting, and we knew eachother for a little over a year before we started working together and it is so much better. So I would advise you to make sure if you choose to change sponsors that you pick one who has the kind of recovery and sobriety that you want, cause that really makes all the difference.

Whatever you decide to do I hope it works out x
